stories.title: Grok Bot ships a Plaid-backed read-only Finance connector: bank, card and investment accounts
stories.summary: SpaceXAI's official @bot account (Sep 26 19:54:25 UTC) launched a Plaid-backed, read-only Finance connector for Grok Bot, letting the persistent computer-use agent pull bank, card and investment accounts to answer spending and investment questions; a same-thread follow-up points to the Bot marketplace where it is listed. This is a new data plane for a persistent agent, not a new model — it extends Grok Bot's connector stack to personal finance. For builders the pattern is the interesting part: a read-only broker between a general agent and financial rails, with 'never sees your logins' and one-click unlink. Caveat: availability is gated to paid Cursor / SuperGrok / Teams / Enterprise Bot plans per the product page, and there is no dedicated x.ai/news post — the X thread is the announcement.

stories.title: SEC Commissioner Hester Peirce sets her last day: Oct 2, 2026
stories.summary: Hester Peirce posted her resignation letter with 'T minus 7' (Sep 25 17:08:59 UTC), fixing her final day at the SEC as October 2, 2026. She led the SEC's Crypto Task Force and has been the commission's most consistent crypto advocate; after her departure the commission is down to two seated members, Atkins and Uyeda. For builders this is the clearest marker yet of how much of the 2026 crypto-rulemaking posture was tied to one commissioner. Caveat: it is a personnel exit, not a rule change; no SEC.gov release was issued, only the letter image on X.

quality.note: Official @HesterPeirce post with her resignation letter; the X post time (17:08:59 UTC) is the publication timestamp. Medium confidence: the date is fixed by her own post, but no SEC.gov release corroborates it.

stories.title: Journal of Physiology: muscle atrophy from aging and disuse is mainly loss of myofibril number, not size
stories.summary: A Journal of Physiology paper (online Sep 25, 2026; promoted by @DMSabatini Sep 26 and @davidasinclair Sep 26) used macroscopic-to-ultrastructural analyses in human and mouse tissue to show that aging- and disuse-induced muscle-fibre atrophy is mediated primarily by a lower number of myofibrils rather than smaller myofibril size, in SERCA1 fibres. For builders of sarcopenia interventions this reframes the target: preserving myofibril number — not just cross-sectional area — is the mechanistic lever. Caveat: it is an observational/mechanism paper, not a trial or therapeutic result, and the authors' own amplification is commentary, not a new finding.

stories.title: Anthropic commits ~$11.6B over seven years to Akamai dedicated cloud compute, with a warrant for up to 387,051 Series B shares
stories.summary: An SEC 8-K filed by Akamai (Sept 24, 2026) discloses that under Project Plans 2 and 3 of the May 5, 2026 master agreement, Anthropic has committed to pay roughly $11.6 billion across two initial seven-year terms for dedicated cloud compute plus managed support, subject to delivery and service-availability requirements and termination rights. The deal also carries a warrant for up to 387,051 Series B non-voting preferred shares at $2,226.60, each convertible into 20 common shares, vesting in tranches tied to $3.0B increments of contractual value. For builders this is a major, contractually-documented AI capacity commitment — the scale of CPU/dedicated-cloud spending around frontier model training and serving. Caveat: the contract date is Sept 18, the public 8-K is Sept 24; TechCrunch's $5.5B capex figure is from its story, not the 8-K body; and neither @AnthropicAI nor @Akamai posted the deal in the window — it surfaced via the filing and Bloomberg.

stories.title: Nature: MMEJ repair at TA repeats maintains oncogenic ecDNA — Polθ inhibition destabilizes it
stories.summary: A peer-reviewed Nature paper (published 23 Sep 2026; @Nature posted it in-window Sep 26 11:34 UTC) shows that microhomology-mediated end joining, not NHEJ or HR, selectively maintains extrachromosomal DNA: TA-rich loci on ecDNA are break hotspots, FANCM suppresses break formation, and ERCC1–ERCC4 cleavage channels breaks into MMEJ. Disrupting FANCM or Polθ destabilizes ecDNA and compromises the fitness of ecDNA-dependent cancers, identifying Polθ inhibition as a strategy to sensitize ecDNA-driven tumours. For longevity-adjacent builders, it is a concrete mechanism for one of the hallmarks of genomic instability that drives aging and cancer. Caveat: it is oncology, not a longevity intervention; the in-window item is Nature's post of the already-published paper.

quality.note: Peer-reviewed open-access Nature article published 23 September 2026 (no clock time on the page, so noon UTC is used as the stated limitation) with the official @Nature post in-window (11:34:14 UTC, Sep 26).

stories.title: Catch-up: Science news — a single wildfire-smoke exposure leaves lasting immune and DNA changes suggesting accelerated aging in macaques
stories.summary: Science's news team reports that rhesus macaques exposed to a single 2020 Oregon wildfire smoke event at the Oregon National Primate Research Center — with no immediate harm — show, now as adolescents, lasting immune changes and DNA modifications (epigenetic-clock shifts) consistent with accelerated aging. For builders this is a natural experiment linking a real environmental stressor to durable molecular aging signatures, relevant to air-pollution and aging research. Caveat: Science's news page describes a bioRxiv preprint posted last month (August 2026) that has not yet been peer-reviewed; it is an animal result, not a human clinical finding, and the live Science page was behind a Cloudflare check at fetch time (dated 22 Sep 2026, 4:40 PM ET via the search index).

stories.title: Catch-up: bioRxiv preprint — transplanted hearts take on the recipient's biological age, without shifting systemic age
stories.summary: A Gladyshev-lab bioRxiv preprint (v1 posted Sep 15, 2026) shows that heterochronic heart grafts in mice, plus human cardiac biopsy data, shift DNA-methylation and expression age of the grafted heart toward the recipient — young hearts age locally, old hearts rejuvenate locally — while the systemic recipient age does not shift in the same direction. This directly tests 'organ replacement as rejuvenation' at the epigenetic level. In-window, @EricTopol highlighted it (Sep 26 15:43 UTC), and the human DNAm set was corrected in-thread to 11 patients, not 400+. Caveat: preprint, not peer-reviewed; mouse models plus a small human biopsy set — correlation, not a treatment trial.

quality.note: bioRxiv preprint (v1 posted 2026-09-15, no clock time, so noon UTC is used as the stated limitation) with the in-window @EricTopol discussion (15:43:20 UTC, Sep 26) as the trigger. stories.title: LeRobot: running humanoid loco-manipulation on a Unitree G1 with a π0.5 policy over SONIC motion tokens
stories.summary: Hugging Face's LeRobot team published 'Bringing Humanoids to LeRobot' (Sep 25, 2026): it wires a Unitree G1 into the open LeRobot stack, where a π0.5 VLA policy predicts SONIC latent motion tokens and a fast whole-body controller on the G1 decodes them into stable 29-DoF motion, building on the OpenHLM whole-body loco-manipulation work. The key architectural point for builders: VLA inference is too slow to control a biped directly, so a fast controller sits between the learned policy and the robot, and useful loco-manipulation saturates at roughly 40 demonstrations per task. Caveat: it is a community blog integration write-up (signed 'The LeRobot team'), not a versioned LeRobot release or new robot; the underlying policies, docs and hardware are already public.

quality.note: Official LeRobot blog post dated September 25, 2026; the page exposes only a date, so noon UTC is used as the stated limitation. Medium confidence: community article, not a versioned release.

stories.title: WB-WAM: open whole-body humanoid loco-manipulation model — 1,880h heterogeneous pretraining, 81.9% on HumanoidArena
stories.summary: The WB-WAM team (Tsinghua, Xiong'an Institute of AI, University of Melbourne) published the official training, data and deployment repository for a whole-body humanoid loco-manipulation world-action model (repo created Sep 25 09:31:32 UTC; project page live). The project page cites 1,880.2 hours of heterogeneous pretraining and an 81.9% mean success rate on seven HumanoidArena tasks, with the real-robot path on a Unitree G1 with Wuji hands. For builders this is another concrete, reproducible whole-body humanoid policy with public data and code. Caveat: the paper link is still 'coming soon' (not yet peer-reviewed), it is one specific G1 + Wuji configuration, and no release tag was verified — the new repo is the event.

quality.note: Official project page and GitHub repo (created 2026-09-25 09:31:32 UTC); the repo-creation time is used as the publication timestamp. Medium confidence: companion paper not yet public.
